questions.explanation: Containers delivered by a cloud provider shift more of the stack (OS, runtime, hardware) to the provider than self-managed VMs do.
optionNotes: IaaS VMs leave the OS to the customer
Right: most responsibility moved to provider
Fully customer-managed
Fully customer-managed

questions.stem: The security operations center (SOC) has received credible intelligence that a threat actor is planning to attack with multiple variants of a destructive virus. After obtaining a sample set of this virus' variants and reverse engineering them to understand how they work, a commonality was found. All variants are coded to write to a specific memory location. It is determined this virus is of no threat to the organization because they had the foresight to enable what feature on all endpoints?
questions.explanation: Malware that writes to a fixed memory address fails when ASLR randomizes address layouts.
optionNotes: Separates processes but does not move addresses
Hardware root of trust
Right: fixed addresses become unpredictable
Does not randomize memory inside the guest

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST significant key management problem due to the number of keys created?
options: Keys are more difficult to provision and revoke
Storage of the keys require increased security
Exponential growth when using asymmetric keys
Exponential growth when using symmetric keys
questions.explanation: Symmetric systems need n(n-1)/2 keys, which grows roughly with the square of the number of users and creates a key-management burden; asymmetric needs only 2n.
optionNotes: Generic, not tied to key count
Generic
Asymmetric scales linearly
Right: symmetric key count explodes

questions.stem: Which of the following security objectives for industrial control systems (ICS) can be adapted to securing any Internet of Things (IoT) system?
options: Restore the system after an incident.
questions.explanation: Protecting individual components from exploitation is a general ICS objective that applies directly to IoT devices, which are often weak components.
optionNotes: Narrower objective
Recovery objective
Detection objective
Right: component hardening generalizes

questions.stem: Which security architecture strategy could be applied to secure an operating system (OS) baseline for deployment within the corporate enterprise?
questions.explanation: Secure defaults means shipping the OS baseline already hardened: unneeded services disabled, secure settings on, default credentials changed. That is exactly what a deployable baseline image provides.
optionNotes: Least privilege is applied to accounts, not the whole baseline.
Separation of duties concerns people and processes.
Correct: a hardened baseline embodies secure defaults.
Fail secure describes behaviour on failure, not baseline configuration.

questions.stem: When adopting software as a service (Saas), which security responsibility will remain with the adopting organization?
questions.explanation: In SaaS the provider runs everything up to the application. The customer still owns its data, so classifying and governing that data remains the customer's job.
optionNotes: The CSP handles physical security.
Correct: the data owner keeps classification duties.
The CSP manages the network.
The SaaS provider controls the application layer.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the weakest form of protection for an application that handles Personally Identifiable Information (PII)?
questions.explanation: RC4 is a broken stream cipher (biased keystream, prohibited in TLS by RFC 7465), so it is the weakest protection listed.
optionNotes: TLS 1.2/1.3 is strong transport protection.
Correct: RC4 is deprecated and insecure.
SAML is a sound federation standard.
MFA greatly strengthens authentication.

questions.stem: Of the following, which BEST provides non- repudiation with regards to access to a server room?
questions.explanation: Biometrics tie entry to a specific person, giving non-repudiation. Fobs and PINs can be shared, and cages give no individual attribution.
optionNotes: Fobs and PINs can be shared or lent.
Cages give no individual record.
Correct: biometrics bind access to the individual.
Proximity cards can be shared or cloned.

questions.stem: What documentation is produced FIRST when performing an effective physical loss control process?
questions.explanation: Physical loss control starts by identifying what you have. The inventory comes first, then valuation, then controls.
optionNotes: Controls are chosen after assets and risks are known.
Standards come after the assets are known.
Correct: inventory is the first step.
Valuation needs the inventory first.

questions.stem: Internet protocol security (IPSec), point-to-point tunneling protocol (PPTP), and secure sockets Layer (SSL) all use Which of the following to prevent replay attacks?
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said D] IPSec (AH/ESP), SSL/TLS and PPTP/GRE all embed sequence numbers in packets/records; receivers reject repeated or out-of-window numbers.
optionNotes: Key length affects brute-force strength, not replay.
"Single integrity protection" is not a defined anti-replay mechanism.
Right: AH/ESP, TLS records and PPTP/GRE all carry sequence numbers checked by the receiver.
Nonces are used in some handshakes but are not the common anti-replay mechanism of all three.

questions.stem: Which of the following system components enforces access controls on an object?
questions.explanation: The reference monitor mediates every subject access to objects; the security kernel implements it.
optionNotes: The perimeter is the boundary of the TCB; it does not enforce access.
The matrix stores rules; it does not enforce them.
A trusted domain is a trust scope, not an enforcer.
Right: the reference monitor mediates all access.

questions.stem: An organization is considering partnering with a third-party supplier of cloud services. The organization will only be providing the data and the third-party supplier will be providing the security controls. Which of the following BEST describes this service offering?
questions.explanation: In SaaS the customer supplies only data while the provider manages the application, platform and the security controls.
optionNotes: In PaaS the customer secures its own applications.
In IaaS the customer secures the OS and above.
Right: the provider runs everything and the customer supplies data.
XaaS is a generic umbrella term.

questions.stem: Which of the following attributes could be used to describe a protection mechanism of an open design methodology?
options: It must be tamperproof to protect it from malicious attacks.
It can facilitate independent confirmation of the design security.
It can facilitate blackbox penetration testing.
It exposes the design to vulnerabilities and malicious attacks.
questions.explanation: Open design (Kerckhoffs) lets security be independently reviewed and confirmed rather than relying on secrecy.
optionNotes: Tamperproofing is a reference monitor property.
Right: a public design allows independent review.
Open design supports white-box review, not black-box testing.
The principle holds that exposure does not weaken a sound design.

questions.stem: An organization is implementing data encryption using symmetric ciphers and the Chief Information Officer (CIO) is concerned about the risk of using one key to protect all sensitive data, The security practitioner has been tasked with recommending a solution to address the CIO's concerns, Which of the following is the BEST approach to achieving the objective by encrypting all sensitive data?
options: Use a hierarchy of encryption keys.
Use Hash Message Authentication Code (HMAC) keys.
questions.explanation: A key hierarchy (KEKs protecting many DEKs) avoids a single key encrypting all data and limits compromise impact.
optionNotes: A hash does not encrypt data.
Right: DEKs wrapped by KEKs, so there is no single key for everything.
HMAC gives integrity, not encryption.
RSA is asymmetric and does not answer the symmetric key-scope concern.

questions.stem: International bodies established a regulatory scheme that defines how weapons are exchanged between the signatories. It also addresses cyber weapons, including malicious software, Command and Control (C2) software, and internet surveillance software. This is a description of which of the following?
questions.explanation: The Wassenaar Arrangement is a multilateral export-control regime for conventional arms and dual-use goods, extended in 2013 to cover intrusion software and IP surveillance tools.
optionNotes: EU privacy regulation, not arms control
UN convention on transnational organized crime
Correct: multilateral export control incl. cyber tools
US-only arms export rule, not an international scheme

questions.stem: Which combination of cryptographic algorithms are compliant with Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) Publication 140-2 for non-legacy systems?
options: Diffie-hellman (DH) key exchange: DH (>=2048 bits) Symmetric Key: Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) > 128 bits Digital Signature: Rivest-Shamir-Adleman (RSA) (1024 bits)
Diffie-hellman (DH) key exchange: DH (>=2048 bits) Symmetric Key: Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) > 128 bits Digital Signature: Digital Signature Algorithm (DSA) (>=2048 bits)
Diffie-hellman (DH) key exchange: DH (<= 1024 bits) Symmetric Key: Blowfish Digital Signature: Rivest-Shamir-Adleman (RSA) (>=2048 bits)
Diffie-hellman (DH) key exchange: DH (>=2048 bits) Symmetric Key: Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) < 128 bits Digital Signature: Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA) (>=256 bits)
questions.explanation: Current approved parameters require DH 2048+, AES with at least 128-bit keys and signatures such as DSA 2048+; RSA-1024, Blowfish and short keys are not acceptable.
optionNotes: RSA-1024 too weak
Correct: all parameters approved
Small DH and Blowfish not approved
AES under 128 bits not valid

questions.stem: Which security feature fully encrypts code and data as it passes to the servers and only decrypts below the hypervisor layer?
questions.explanation: Trusted execution environments (confidential computing) keep code and data encrypted in memory and decrypt only inside the protected hardware enclave below the hypervisor.
optionNotes: Protects data at rest only
Protects in transit only
Manages keys, does not compute
Correct: TEE/enclave keeps data encrypted until inside protected hardware

questions.stem: Which would result in the GREATEST impact following a breach to a cloud environment?
options: The hypervisor host is poorly secured
The same Logical Unit Number (LUN) is used for all VMs
questions.explanation: Compromise of the hypervisor exposes every guest VM on that host, so it has the largest blast radius.
optionNotes: Correct: all guests exposed
Storage issue, smaller impact
Limits lateral movement only
Affects single VMs

questions.stem: What is the benefit of an operating system (OS) feature that is designed to prevent an application from executing code from a non-executable memory region?
options: Identifies which security patches still need to be installed on the system
Stops memory resident viruses from propagating their payload
Reduces the risk of polymorphic viruses from encrypting their payload
Helps prevent certain exploits that store code in buffers
questions.explanation: Data Execution Prevention marks buffers non-executable, blocking exploits that inject code into stack/heap.
optionNotes: Patch management
Not specifically
Not related
Correct: DEP/NX blocks code injected into buffers

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST ensures the integrity of transactions to intended recipients?
questions.explanation: PKI provides digital signatures and certificates binding keys to identities, ensuring integrity and authenticity to intended recipients at scale.
optionNotes: Correct: signatures plus certificates bind integrity to identities
Not general solution
No per-identity assurance
Decentralised, weaker trust
